title: Reset waveform hypotheses and data digest (draft)
summary: Draft digest of multi-node short GPU resets observed 2026-12-06 -> 2026-12-07. Collates telemetry signals, preliminary hypotheses (power transients / PCIe AER / NVLink link flap), actions taken during incident, and a minimal runbook for short-term mitigation.
body:
Context:

We observed a correlated cluster of short-duration GPU resets across three racks in cluster-prod-eu between 2026-12-06 22:14 UTC and 2026-12-07 02:03 UTC. Behavior differs from prior ECC-only spikes: resets were brief (1–3s), often followed by successful reinitialization and resumed workloads, but caused request errors and degraded tail-latency for multi-tenant jobs.

High-level numbers (preliminary):
- Affected hosts: 18 physical machines (out of 720 in cluster-prod-eu)
- Affected GPUs: 34 (some hosts have >1 GPU, some single-GPU)
- Incident window: ~3.75 hours, with concentrated bursts around 22:30–23:10 UTC and 00:45–01:05 UTC
- Percentage of jobs impacted in window: ~0.9% of inference requests (skewed to long-chat workloads)

Observed signals and notable traces (raw telemetry highlights):
- Kernel logs: repeated GPU reset messages (driver-level logs show short reset events; message shape looks like 'gpu: reset detected, firmware reinit, pci bus reset sequence started') but not the classic persistent Xid crash pattern we've seen before.
- PCIe AER counters: correctable AER counts ticked up on some hosts minutes before reset bursts.
- System power telemetry: 2 PDUs show micro-second scale current spikes correlated within 5–10s of reset bursts.
- NVLink: intermittent link-down / link-flap entries on 6 GPUs; not all GPUs with NVLink showed link-flap.
- ECC: correctable ECC error rate rose modestly on ~12 GPUs; uncorrectable ECC was not a clear driver.
- FRU/firmware/driver state: mixed driver versions in fleet (some hosts on 560.42, some on 560.51). Nodes with 560.51 show marginally higher reset rate in this sample (approx +18%), but sample size small.

Preliminary hypotheses (ranked by how well they match signals):
1) Power transient triggering watchdog reset: sudden short current spikes at PDU level cause GPU voltage rail instability -> driver sees instability -> brief reset and reinit. Matches PDU spikes and near-simultaneous resets.
2) PCIe AER cascade: increasing correctable AER counts cause chip/host to trigger PCIe reset path. Some nodes show AER drift minutes before resets.
3) NVLink negotiation failure under heavy cross-GPU workload -> firmware triggers protective reset to re-establish link. Correlates with link-flap logs on subset.
4) Driver/firmware mismatch edge-case: driver 560.51 has a watchdog sensitivity regression under particular sequence of NVLink+PCIe events, making resets more likely. Observationally plausible but unproven.

What we tried during the incident (chronological):
- Immediate: auto-eviction of nodes with >3 resets in 5m (prevented repeated client failures).
- Mid-incident: rolled back a suspect canary host from driver 560.51 -> 560.42 (manual), observed no immediate reoccurrence on that host for the remainder of window.
- Power ops: PDUs on the two suspect rows were power-cycled for a narrow maintenance window (tactical), which temporarily reduced event rate in the immediate neighbors.
- NVLink isolation: on 4 hosts with repeated link-flap, we disabled NVLink at the host level (BIOS/driver flags) as an experiment; resets stopped for those hosts. This reduced throughput for some workloads, so we reverted after short test.

Gaps in evidence / open questions:
- PDU telemetry sampling rate is low (1s bins) — microsecond transient details are missing. Need power-hardware team to pull raw logs (BMC/PDU high-res) for the suspect window.
- Are thermal cycling or ambient power events contributing (data-center UPS logs)?
- Does driver 560.51 contain a regression that maps to our workload pattern? Need repro in lab with exact workload and driver/firmware pairing.
- NVLink firmware version distribution across affected GPUs is partially unknown; need hardware asset inventory match.

Suggested short-term mitigations (operational, low risk):
- Eviction policy: implement automatic eviction when node has >=2 resets in 10m (currently >=3 in 5m). Rationale: reduce user-visible failures earlier.
- Fleet driver rollback: temporarily hold canary image rollouts (stop 560.51 expansion) and schedule a controlled rollback plan for fleet nodes with the most resets.
- Power soft-mitigation: stagger PDUs' nonessential loads to reduce transient coupling on suspect rows; request PDU vendor to enable high-res logging for 24–48h.
- NVLink conservative mode: add an infra flag to disable NVLink aggregation for high-risk node pools (costly for throughput but useful for isolation).

Runbook sketch (short checklist for oncall run-through):
1) Detect: alert triggers when cluster-level reset-rate > threshold OR node-level reset_count >= 2 in 10m.
2) Triage: pull kernel log sample, PCIe AER counters, NVLink link status, PDU current trace for last 5 min.
3) Quarantine: cordon + drain node if resets keep happening; if transient and <2 resets, mark for observation.
4) Quick mitigations: toggle NVLink off (if node has NVLink), move workloads off to less-loaded hosts, escalate to power-ops if PDU spikes seen.
5) Rolling rollback: if driver version correlated, schedule controlled rollback of that driver in 50-node canary, watch; if rollback stops resets, expand.
6) Lab repro: create lab job with matching driver/firmware, reproduce with high PCIe stress tool + cross-GPU NVLink traffic, instrument with high-res power logger.

Longer-term work (owner suggestions):
- (Maya) Coordinate with power/hw team to enable microsecond-resolution logging for PDUs and UPS in suspect racks (target: 2026-12-14).
- (Luca) Build a synthetic workload to stress PCIe AER + NVLink negotiation; try to reproduce on a 2-node lab cluster with identical firmware/driver pairings (target: 2026-12-11).
- (Priya) Inventory firmware versions across fleet and cross-reference with resets; build a small board to track firmware vs driver vs reset-rate (target: 2026-12-12).
- (Evan) Draft a minimal SLO change for node eviction policy and run the safety review with Platform (target: 2026-12-09).

Decision tree notes (for post-incident refinement):
- If high-res power logs show sub-ms current spikes aligned to resets -> treat as power-transient root cause; plan hardware PDU replacement or isolation retrofit.
- If lab repro with driver 560.51 reproduces reset without PDU spikes -> treat as driver regression (engaging driver vendor/vendor-firmware path).
- If disabling NVLink prevents resets in lab and prod -> consider NVLink firmware update / runbook to isolate NVLink-heavy workloads to specialized pools.

Ancillary observations (non-blocking but useful):
- Affected customer types were mostly long-chat workloads with multi-turn context (high KV cache usage). That workload leads to sustained KV cache memory footprint and cross-GPU communication which magnifies NVLink/PCIe sensitivity.
- There are a few historical incidents where transient PDU noise preceded ECC bursts (see linked JIRA HW-78); this seems like a related syndrome but different manifestation (resets vs ECC-only).

Immediate action items (within 48h):
- [Maya] File PDU high-res log request with data-center ops (ETA 48h).
- [Luca] Stand up lab repro harness and attempt initial reproduction (ETA 48h).
- [Priya] Generate firmware/driver distribution snapshot for cluster-prod-eu and mark nodes with mismatched pairings (ETA 24h).
- [Evan] Propose change to auto-eviction threshold and open RFC for emergency rollback guardrails (ETA 24h).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Term we should use for this pattern: "reset waveform" (captures repeated, short resets that form bursts) — avoids conflation with persistent kernel panics or ECC storms.
- Consider synthesizing a small visualization for the incident: stacked timeline with per-node resets, PDU current traces, and PCIe AER counter overlay. This is high value for postmortem audience.

Unresolved for postmortem:
- definitive root cause (power vs driver vs NVLink) remains unknown. We must not prematurely label.
- quantify customer impact precisely (request logging + replay).

Appendix: useful commands / log extraction snippets (for oncall):
- kernel logs: sudo journalctl -k --since "2026-12-06 22:00" | grep -E "gpu|AER|NVLink|reset"
- PCIe AER counters: sudo ./pcie-aer-dump.sh --host $(hostname) --since 2026-12-06T22:00
- NVLink status: sudo nvidia-smi nvlink --query -l 1 --format=csv
- driver version: modinfo nvidia | grep version

End of draft. Use this to guide the postmortem run. Keep this doc as working draft until lab repro or PDU evidence nails the root cause.
